messages:
Ivy R: Anyone else getting CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED when using the python SDK inside a Windows venv on 3.11? Works fine on Linux and our CI (3.10).
Ivy R: Minimal repro: create venv with python.org 3.11.4, pip install redwood-sdk==0.7.0, then simple client call fails during TLS handshake.
Sam G: Which SSL backend shows up (`ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION`)? Some windows builds bundle OpenSSL and bypass the Windows cert store.
Ivy R: Shows OpenSSL 3.0.10. I thought python.org used Windows cert store, but this looks like it prefers the bundled CA file.
Nina C: Quick workaround: `pip install certifi` and either set SSL_CERT_FILE to `certifi.where()` or create an `ssl.SSLContext(cafile=certifi.where())` and pass it to the client if supported.
Ivy R: Setting SSL_CERT_FILE fixed my local repro. Can we make the SDK respect SSL_CERT_FILE first and fall back to system certs?
Sam G: Yes we should. Also add an `ssl_context` param on AsyncClient/Client so callers can pass an explicit context. I can open a draft PR to change the HTTP layer precedence: env -> certifi -> bundled -> system.
Ivy R: That would be great. Please also add a short note to the Windows quickstart and a changelog entry. This tripped up an internal onboarding sample.
ops-bot: Created TICKET-2784: "py-sdk windows venv cert precedence (py3.11)" - https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/TICKET-2784 :white_check_mark:
Sam G: Draft PR link (wip): https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/220 - exposes ssl_context, checks SSL_CERT_FILE, prefers certifi when installed, and updates type stubs.
Nina C: I'll validate the branch on our Windows lab across 3.8-3.12 and confirm the fix. If green, we can cut a 0.7.1 patch and publish the quickstart docs update.
Ivy R: Thanks all, saved my onboarding demo. Leaving thread until patch + docs are merged. :thumbsup:
